title: Design a Gaming Leaderboard
relevance: High — Alex Xu System Design Interview Vol.2 Ch.10 classic; common at Meta / Google / PayPal / Amazon gaming & social rounds; tests Redis sorted sets, atomic increments, sharding, and real-time vs eventual consistency.
company_notes: Campus/new-grad: common shorter HLD as a Redis data-structure pick once caching is known, often lighter than feed/chat. Experienced (1–4+ YOE): Meta / Google / PayPal / Amazon (gaming, social, fantasy sports) with depth on sharding, durability, friends boards, and anti-cheat. High frequency among Vol.2-style questions; treat as mandatory after caching foundations and before heavier designs like payments or stock exchange.

phases.goal: Lock ByteByteGo-style FRs/NFRs, scale class, clarifications, and out-of-scope lines before designing.

must_hit.point: Functional core: display top 10 (or top K), return a specific user's rank + score, and update scores server-side when a player wins a match.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names top-K board, per-user rank+score, and server-side match-driven score updates.

must_hit.point: NFRs: near-real-time rank visibility (not nightly batch), top-K and rank reads ≪ 100 ms p99, and durability enough to rebuild after Redis loss.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States near-real-time, sub-100 ms p99 reads, and rebuild-after-Redis-loss durability.

must_hit.point: Default scale class ~5M DAU / ~25M MAU unless the interviewer overrides.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Anchors design talk to ~5M DAU / ~25M MAU.

must_hit.point: Clarify score model (wins = +1 vs XP), real-time vs batch, monthly reset, tie-break, friends/regional boards, anti-cheat; bonus ±4 neighbors around a user.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Asks the clarify-first product questions and mentions optional neighbor window.

must_hit.point: Out of scope unless asked: matchmaking ELO math, anti-cheat ML, and full social graph.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly parks ELO, ML anti-cheat, and full social graph.

probes: What are the functional and non-functional requirements, default scale, and what are you leaving out of scope?

hints.1: Separate must-have top-K and my-rank from optional neighbors/friends/windows.
hints.2: State near-real-time + ≪ 100 ms p99 reads, then name the default DAU/MAU.
hints.3: Core: top 10/K + user rank/score + server-side updates; NFR near-real-time ≪ 100 ms p99; ~5M DAU / ~25M MAU; park ELO/ML/full graph.

phases.goal: Derive score-update QPS, read QPS, and ZSET memory to show a single Redis node is enough at default scale.

must_hit.point: Assume 5M DAU / 25M MAU and about 10 matches per user per day.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States 5M/25M and 10 matches/user/day out loud.

must_hit.point: Score-update QPS ≈ ~500/s average and peak ~2.5k/s; top-10 fetch QPS ≈ ~50/s (reads cheap vs writes).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Quotes ~500/s avg, ~2.5k/s peak writes, and ~50/s top-10 reads.

must_hit.point: ZSET memory ~26 B/member × 25M ≈ ~650 MB, plus skip-list overhead ≈ ~1–2 GB — one Redis node at this scale.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks ~26 B × 25M → ~650 MB and ~1–2 GB with overhead, concludes one node.

must_hit.point: At 5M DAU a single Redis ZSET is enough; sharding is the 100× scale deep dive (500M DAU → ~65 GB, ~250k QPS).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says single ZSET at 5M DAU and reserves sharding for 500M DAU / ~65 GB / ~250k QPS.

probes: Walk the Alex Xu-style back-of-envelope: DAU, match rate, score-update QPS, and ZSET memory — do we need to shard yet?

hints.1: Start from DAU/MAU and matches per user per day before QPS.
hints.2: Compute write QPS and ZSET memory, then conclude single-node vs shard.
hints.3: 5M/25M, 10 matches/day → ~500/s avg / ~2.5k/s peak writes; ~650 MB–~1–2 GB → one Redis node; shard at 500M DAU.

phases.goal: Define server-only score writes and public top-K / rank / optional neighbor read APIs.

must_hit.point: Internal write only from game servers: POST /v1/scores with body {user_id, points} → 200 OK | 400; not callable by public clients.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows POST /v1/scores as game-server-only and returns 200/400.

must_hit.point: GET /v1/scores returns top 10 entries with user_id, user_name, rank, and score.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes public top-10 list payload with rank and score fields.

must_hit.point: GET /v1/scores/{user_id} returns that user's score and rank.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the per-user rank+score read endpoint.

must_hit.point: Optional: GET /v1/scores/{user_id}/neighbors?k=4 for players around the user; later GET with window=weekly or /friends.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions neighbors?k=4 and optional weekly/friends reads.

probes: What are the write and read APIs, and who is allowed to call the score write?

hints.1: Keep score writes off public clients.
hints.2: Separate internal POST from public GET top-K and GET-by-user.
hints.3: POST /v1/scores (game servers only); GET /v1/scores top 10; GET /v1/scores/{id}; optional neighbors?k=4.

phases.goal: Model Redis hot ranking keys plus a durable point log that can rebuild the ZSET.

must_hit.point: Redis hot path: key leaderboard:{yyyy_mm} is a ZSET of user_id → score.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names monthly ZSET key and member=user_id / score=points.

must_hit.point: Durable store: users(user_id PK, display_name, ...) and points(user_id, delta, created_at, match_id?) as audit/rebuild source; replay points into a new ZSET on failover.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows users + points tables and rebuild-by-replay.

must_hit.point: Optional Hash user:{id} for name/avatar metadata, or cache only top-K profiles.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates profile Hash/cache from the ranking ZSET.

must_hit.point: Windowed keys like lb:daily:{date}, lb:weekly:{iso_week}, lb:alltime; writes amplify across active windows; EXPIRE on ephemeral daily/weekly keys.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists per-window keys, write amplification, and EXPIRE on ephemeral windows.

probes: What lives in Redis vs the durable DB, and how do time-windowed boards map to keys?

hints.1: Redis holds the ranked projection; DB holds the rebuildable history.
hints.2: One ZSET key per leaderboard window, plus optional profile Hash.
hints.3: leaderboard:{yyyy_mm} ZSET; users + points for rebuild; lb:daily/weekly/alltime with EXPIRE on ephemeral keys.

phases.goal: Place authoritative game validation, leaderboard service, Redis ZSET, and durable DB on write and read paths.

must_hit.point: Write path: Client → Game Service validates match → Leaderboard Service → Redis ZINCRBY and durable DB (async or dual-write).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws game-authoritative validation then ZINCRBY + durable append.

must_hit.point: Read path: Client → Leaderboard Service → Redis (ZREVRANGE / ZREVRANK) then enrich names/avatars from user DB or profile cache.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows Redis rank/range reads plus profile enrichment.

must_hit.point: Durability split: Redis is the hot ranking projection; RDBMS/event log is source of truth for point history and ZSET rebuild.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States Redis projection vs DB/event-log source of truth.

must_hit.point: Optional Kafka (or queue) between game and leaderboard when analytics, push, or multiple consumers need the same score event.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Inserts an optional queue for fan-out consumers without making it mandatory.

probes: Sketch the write and read paths — where is the score authored, and what is Redis vs the DB for?

hints.1: Game service owns match truth; clients never write ranks.
hints.2: Leaderboard service dual-writes Redis + durable log; reads hit Redis then enrich.
hints.3: Validate → (optional queue) → ZINCRBY + points row; reads ZREVRANGE/ZREVRANK + profile store.

phases.goal: Defend Redis ZSET over SQL, atomic increments, sharding strategy, freshness, and exact vs approximate Top-K.

must_hit.point: Reject SQL ORDER BY / nested COUNT(*) rank for real-time millions of players (O(N) under continuous updates); Redis ZSET keeps order on write with O(log N) insert/update/rank/range.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts O(N) SQL ranking with ZSET order-on-write O(log N).

must_hit.point: Prefer ZINCRBY (or Lua) over get-score → add → set so concurrent match completions cannot lose increments.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists on atomic ZINCRBY and rejects non-atomic RMW.

must_hit.point: Sharding tradeoff: fixed score-range partitions make top-K hit one shard but players migrate on score change; hash/Redis Cluster makes writes easy but top-K needs scatter-gather merge and exact global ZREVRANK is hard.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compares fixed-range locality vs hash-slot scatter-gather and hard global rank.

must_hit.point: Consistency: Redis primary for live ranks (accept replica lag); DB for durability; seconds of lag usually OK for games unless prize payouts need strong consistency.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates live Redis ranks from durable DB and accepts seconds of lag for normal play.

must_hit.point: Exact gaming ranks vs approximate Top-K/trending (Count-Min Sketch / heavy-hitters): know when the interviewer pivots to fuzzy trending.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Distinguishes exact player ranks from approximate trending Top-K.

probes: Why not SQL ORDER BY? How do you update scores atomically? How would you shard, and is exact global rank still cheap?

hints.1: Interviewers will poke SQL ranking and concurrent increments first.
hints.2: Then force the fixed-range vs hash-shard top-K/rank tradeoff.
hints.3: ZSET O(log N) + ZINCRBY; fixed-range vs Cluster scatter-gather; Redis live / DB durable; exact ranks ≠ approximate trending.

phases.goal: Scale past single-node Redis, hot top-K reads, shard rank costs, HA loss, write bursts, and abuse.

must_hit.point: Single-node ceiling is memory (~tens of GB comfortable) and write QPS; past that, shard.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names memory/QPS as the ceiling and sharding as the next step.

must_hit.point: Hot top-K reads: cache serialized top-10 JSON with short TTL or pub-sub invalidate; enrich profiles for top players only.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Caches top-10 payload and limits profile enrichment to top players.

must_hit.point: Hash-shard top-K: parallel ZREVRANGE 0 K-1 per shard then merge-sort in app; exact rank needs local rank plus counts on other shards (expensive) or approximate percentile for deep ranks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes scatter-gather top-K merge and expensive exact cross-shard rank.

must_hit.point: Redis HA: primary + replica with AOF/RDB; rebuild from DB if both lost; score-range shards need user→score map and ZREM/ZADD on boundary cross.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Covers replica/AOF/RDB, DB rebuild, and score-range migration ops.

must_hit.point: Write bursts (tournament finals): queue + batch consumers and shed non-critical neighbor queries; limit active windows and expire old daily keys; only trusted game servers POST /scores with idempotent match_id.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions queueing under finals, window write-amp control, and trusted/idempotent writes.

probes: What breaks first as you grow, and how do top-K and exact rank work once the ZSET is sharded?

hints.1: Start from single-node memory/QPS before inventing a cluster.
hints.2: Cover top-10 caching, scatter-gather top-K, and HA/rebuild.
hints.3: Shard past tens-of-GB/QPS; cache top-10; parallel ZREVRANGE+merge; primary/replica + DB rebuild; trusted idempotent POST /scores.

tradeoffs.topic: SQL ORDER BY vs Redis ZSET
tradeoffs.strong_answer: SQL sorting/nested rank COUNT on read is O(N) and thrashs under continuous score updates because every write invalidates cached order. A Redis ZSET maintains order on write with hash-table ZSCORE O(1) and skip-list O(log N) insert/update/rank/range — the interview default for real-time millions of players.

tradeoffs.topic: ZINCRBY (or Lua) vs get-score → add → set
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Non-atomic read-modify-write loses increments when concurrent matches complete for the same user. ZINCRBY (or a Lua script) makes the increment atomic so concurrent completions cannot drop points.

tradeoffs.topic: Fixed score-range shards vs Redis Cluster hash slots
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Fixed score-range partitions keep global top-K on one shard but force player migration (ZREM/ZADD) when scores cross boundaries. Hash/Cluster sharding makes writes easy, but top-K needs scatter-gather merge from every shard and exact global ZREVRANK is expensive — often approximate or backed by a secondary aggregator.

tradeoffs.topic: Exact gaming ranks vs approximate Top-K / trending
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Gaming leaderboards usually need exact positions for a player (ZSET ranks). Approximate structures like Count-Min Sketch / heavy-hitters fit trending or huge write fan-in where fuzzy Top-K is acceptable — a different problem than exact match leaderboards.

tradeoffs.topic: Redis live ranks vs DB durability / freshness
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Use Redis as the hot ranking projection for low-latency live ranks and the RDBMS/event log as source of truth for rebuild. Accept seconds of replica/queue lag for ordinary games; require stronger consistency only when prize payouts depend on exact fresh ranks.

gotchas.trap: Leaving tie-break undefined when two players share a score
gotchas.correction: State competition vs dense vs unique ranking; Redis default unique order is lexicographic on member id, or use a composite score (points + inverted timestamp).

gotchas.trap: Letting the client write scores directly
gotchas.correction: Never; only the game service validates the match and the leaderboard service updates — stops MITM/cheat proxies.

gotchas.trap: Treating Redis as the sole source of truth
gotchas.correction: If Redis dies, ranks must rebuild from a durable point log/DB snapshot; Redis is a hot projection with replica/failover, not the only store.

gotchas.trap: Maintaining a ZSET per user for friends boards
gotchas.correction: Do not N-way fan-out ZSETs; pipeline ZSCORE for friend IDs and sort locally, or keep small per-clique boards if the graph is hot.

gotchas.trap: One ZSET for daily, weekly, and all-time together
gotchas.correction: Use one ZSET key per window, EXPIRE ephemeral daily/weekly keys, and write to all active windows (accepting write amplification).

gotchas.trap: Claiming a single ZSET still works at 500M DAU
gotchas.correction: Must shard; walk fixed score-range vs Cluster hash and the scatter-gather tax on global top-K (~65 GB, ~250k QPS class).

gotchas.trap: Answering with approximate Top-K / trending sketches for exact player ranks
gotchas.correction: Gaming ranks usually need exact positions; reserve Count-Min / heavy-hitters for trending-style pivots.
